---
title: "Week 5 self-check — reproduce and transfer"
---

Use these questions to check the whole workflow and locate any unfinished
practical skills. They are not a graded test. Remote tasks requiring an account
remain pending until the actual course service is provided.

## 1. Name the location, not just the filename

Your report rendered remotely, but local Downloads is empty. What should you
check? Does closing the SSH terminal necessarily delete saved remote output?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Locate the output on the remote computer, then check whether it was transferred
and to which destination. A remote desktop is not automatic synchronisation.
Closing SSH ends a session, not saved files, subject to the service's storage
policy. Do not assume a running process will continue after disconnecting.
:::

## 2. Count the represented thing

`dna <- readLines("data/dna.txt")` reads one invented 40-letter line. What are
`length(dna)` and `nchar(dna)`? Why do they differ?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

`length(dna)` is **1** stored string; `nchar(dna)` is **40** characters in that
string. Counting vector elements and counting characters answer different
questions. The final newline in the file is not another DNA base.
:::

## 3. Pixels are positions, not plants

The teaching image has 64 pixels, 24 above intensity 100. What fraction is bright?
Does that make 64 independent biological replicates or identify one cell?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

The fraction is **24/64 = 0.375**. Pixels are related positions in one artificial
image. Their count does not establish independent treatment replication or
biological identity. Interpretation needs acquisition context, scale, and
validation. The threshold count alone does not establish a cell's area in mm².
:::

## 4. Available duckweed measurements

Twenty independent flasks were started, ten per allocation. Nutrient flask F17
spilled before weighing. How many available biomass observations are there, and
why is replacing the missing value by zero inappropriate?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

There are **10 control and 9 nutrient observations**, 19 in total. Zero would
invent a known biomass; unavailable and absent biomass are different meanings.
Retain the original row, report the loss, and make the comparison conditional
on the observed data and missingness limitation.
:::

## 5. A percentage difference needs its units

In the supplied alternative, percentage yield is `100 × collected mass / supplied
maximum mass`, with matching mass units. Protocol means are 68.67% and 77.00%.
Is their difference an 8.33% relative increase? Does it establish greater purity?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

The modified-minus-standard difference is **8.33 percentage points**. A relative
percentage change would divide by the starting mean and multiply by 100; it is
a different quantity. Greater yield alone does not establish greater purity,
safety, sustainability, or general superiority. Product purity was an explicit
simplifying assumption in this numerical exercise, not a measured finding.
:::

## 6. Share a recipe, not only its output

A peer receives your HTML but cannot update the analysis for new data. What
else should be in the shared project? Why test extraction in a new location?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Include the `.Rmd` source, actual input CSV, dictionary, project file, required
output folder if used, and a short README naming packages and the file to render.
Testing a new location detects dependencies on personal absolute paths or missing
files. The `.Rproj` does not contain the dataset. A fresh session detects hidden
interactive objects. Do not include credentials or unrelated personal work.
:::

## 7. What does successful reproduction establish?

The peer renders your source successfully from the shared input. Does that prove
the experimental design and interpretation are correct, or provide a backup
against losing your only disk?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

It establishes that the supplied work regenerates the result in the tested
environment. A flawed analysis can be reproducible. Scientific validity still
needs the design, assumptions, checks, and reasoning. Backup is a separate action:
keep a retrievable copy using supported separate storage.
:::

## 8. Checks have limits

The received table has the same filename, byte size, row count, and column names
as the source. Does this prove that every measurement matches? What would you
check in a small transfer audit before making a stronger claim?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. A changed value can occupy the same number of characters, and tables can
have identical dimensions but different contents. Inspect the intended saved
input, verify named records and missing values, and compare the contents using
the supported method. Record the actual source and destination locations.
Do not confuse an unsaved editor change with the bytes that were sent.
:::

## 9. One changed label, one unchanged length

The invented DNA string has A11, C9, G9, T11. Its first A is replaced by G in
a new object. What are the changed A/G counts, total length, and GC fraction,
defined here as (G + C) / all letters? Did the original file necessarily change?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer and calculation

A10 and G10, still 40 letters, with GC fraction `(10 + 9) / 40 = 0.475`.
The original fraction was `18 / 40 = 0.45`. Changing a new R object does not
write a file unless a save/write operation is performed. A count-based fraction
does not establish what a DNA sequence does biologically.
:::

## 10. A threshold can change its answer without moving an object

The toy image has 24 pixels at 210 and 40 at 25. Add 30 to every intensity in
a new object. Compare counts above 220 before and after. What about counts
above 100? Explain the difference between `> 210` and `>= 210` in the original.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Above 220 changes from zero to 24 because the bright pixels become 240. Above
100 stays at 24. Original `> 210` excludes equality and selects zero, whereas
`>= 210` selects 24. Matrix positions did not change, so a threshold-count change
alone cannot establish a larger organism or a change in physical object area.
:::

## 11. A fresh dataset requires fresh counts

The algae table has 24 independent cultures, twelve per allocation. A19 in the
supplement group spilled before weighing. Its available group means are 28.20
mg for reference and 33.91818 mg for supplement. Give available n and the
observed supplement-minus-reference difference. Must supplement contain the
largest single observation?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer and calculation

Available n is **12 reference and 11 supplement**, 23 in total. The directed
difference is `33.91818 - 28.20 ≈ 5.72 mg`. A higher group mean does not require
every value to be higher: reference culture A11 at 41.7 mg is the largest
individual observation. Describe both the centre and observations.
:::

## 12. A sensitivity check does not justify deletion

Omitting A11 lowers the algae reference mean to 26.97273 mg and increases the
observed difference to about 6.95 mg. No source record identifies A11 as an
error. Which result should be primary, and how should the other be labelled?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Keep the **all-available-measurements result** primary: about 5.72 mg. The
other is a diagnostic sensitivity calculation with an explicitly changed sample
and no independent evidence for exclusion. Reweighing preferences or a more
convenient p-value cannot justify removing a recorded observation. A19 remains
a distinct missing measurement; omitting A11 does not repair that loss.
:::

## 13. Rendering can miss the more serious fault

In a disposable report copy, an input is temporarily renamed. In another copy,
the prose claims that every enrolled duckweed flask had a measured outcome.
Which fault should stop rendering, and which may render successfully?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

The unchanged input path should fail when its required file is unavailable.
Restore its exact name/path, rerun, and compare the result. The false prose can
render successfully because software does not automatically validate the claim.
It contradicts the documented missing F17 measurement. Check scientific meaning
as well as execution; keep intentionally faulty copies out of the final package.
:::

## 14. Is this a rounding difference or a different analysis?

One memo gives a mean of 33.91818 mg and the report displays 33.92 mg. Another
report gives 34.32 mg. What should be investigated, and why should you check the
input and calculation before changing display precision?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

33.92 is the first value rounded to two decimal places. 34.32 is not explained
by that rounding. Check the saved input, available counts, group selection,
outcome definition, and calculation, then confirm which rendered file was opened.
Changing the number of displayed digits cannot repair a different input or an
unrecorded exclusion. Retain full-precision values for subsequent calculations.
:::
